_comment: Authored summary targets — plan.md §9. Keyed by dataset record id. Merge with: npm --prefix api run merge:dataset
_batch: 003 — Hinglish depth. Every record carries a code-mixed note, so the model sees translation-and-mark on RED and AMBER cases as well as the easy ones. Several carry a genuine tension between the note and the tick-box answers.
red_cauda_equina-003:
**Snapshot** — 48y woman, farm and labour work. Lower back pain with leg pain and numbness, 6 weeks to 3 months.

**Key findings**
- Saddle numbness reported — inner thighs and the area she sits on
- Pain radiates below the knee
- Bladder and bowel control both reported intact
- No weakness; walking unrestricted; pain 5/10
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Saddle sensory change alone triggers the cauda equina screen. A moderate pain score and normal bladder answers do not soften it.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- When the saddle numbness began, and whether it is spreading
- Urinary hesitancy or loss of the sensation of bladder filling
- Perianal sensation and anal tone on examination
- She wrote *(translated)*: "I had shown a doctor before, they told me to do exercises. It did not help at all."
red_progressive_deficit-001:
**Snapshot** — 44y woman, farm and labour work. Lower back pain with leg pain and weakness, 6 weeks to 3 months, getting worse.

**Key findings**
- Leg or foot weakness worsening quickly, or the foot dragging
- Difficulty standing on toes and heels
- Pain radiates below the knee
- Bladder, bowel and saddle sensation reported normal
- Still working, with difficulty

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Weakness that is progressing rather than static drives the urgency, independent of a moderate pain score.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- How quickly the weakness has advanced — days or weeks
- Power by myotome, ankle dorsiflexion in particular
- She wrote *(translated)*: "It would be better if the whole check-up could be done in one visit, coming again and again is difficult." Manual work and travel cost may limit follow-up — worth front-loading investigations.
red_myelopathy-005:
**Snapshot** — 62y woman, shop or business. Neck pain with arm pain and numbness, 3 to 12 months, getting worse.

**Key findings**
- Fine-motor loss — buttoning, coins, writing all harder
- Both hands affected; objects slip from the grip
- Pain and numbness below the elbow
- Now needs some help with dressing and bathing
- Gait steady; no urinary urgency

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Loss of dexterity with bilateral hand involvement suggests a pattern consistent with cord compression rather than a single root.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Hoffmann's, inverted supinator, and lower-limb reflexes
- How quickly function has declined this month
- She wrote *(translated)*: "Everyone in my family has this same problem. My father also had back pain." She may be framing this as familial back pain rather than a new neck problem.
red_infection-003:
**Snapshot** — 68y man, farm and labour work. Lower back pain for 2 to 6 weeks, 8/10.

**Key findings**
- Fever alongside the back pain
- Pain wakes him at night; sleep disturbed most nights
- Diabetes
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation or neurological findings
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Fever with spinal pain in a diabetic, with night pain on top, raises a query of spinal infection. Severity is high for so short a history.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Temperature, and how long the fever has run
- Any recent skin infection, injection or dental work
- Percussion tenderness over the spine
- He wrote *(translated)*: "A hot compress gives a little relief but only for a short while."
red_malignancy-003:
**Snapshot** — 65y woman, homemaker. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 7/10.

**Key findings**
- Previously treated for cancer
- Unintentional weight loss
- Pain wakes her at night; sleep disturbed most nights
- Pain stays in the back — no neurological symptoms
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — A cancer history together with night pain and weight loss is the combination that raises a query of metastatic disease.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Which primary, when treated, and whether she remains under follow-up
- How much weight, over what period
- Imaging the whole spine rather than the painful segment alone
- She wrote *(translated)*: "It would be better if the whole check-up could be done in one visit." Arrange investigations in a single attendance if possible.
red_fracture_trauma-002:
**Snapshot** — 68y man, retired. Lower back pain for under 2 weeks following a fall, 8/10.

**Key findings**
- Recent fall, with onset dated to it
- Severe pain of very recent onset
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Relieved by lying down; sleep undisturbed
- No imaging yet

**Supporting the triage verdict** — A fall at 68 with severe new back pain warrants imaging before the outpatient appointment rather than after it.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Mechanism and height of the fall
- Point tenderness over a spinous process
- Bone health — previous fractures, steroid use, osteoporosis assessment
- He wrote *(translated)*: "Travelling is very difficult, sitting in a bus or auto is hard." Consider how he will manage getting to imaging.
red_fragility_fracture-003:
**Snapshot** — 74y woman, Bhopal. Lower back pain for 2 to 6 weeks with no clear cause, 8/10.

**Key findings**
- Severe pain of recent onset with no injury reported
- Known brittle bones
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Relieved by lying down; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Sudden severe pain without trauma at 74 with osteoporosis raises a query of vertebral fragility fracture. An acute mechanical pattern also matched; the fracture query outranks it.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Whether pain began during an ordinary movement — bending, coughing, standing
- Any height loss or new stoop noticed by family
- Point tenderness over a spinous process
- She wrote *(translated)*: "A hot compress helps a little but only briefly."
amber_lumbar_radiculopathy-002:
**Snapshot** — 61y man, shop or business. Lower back and leg pain with numbness, 3 to 12 months, 7/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain radiates below the knee on the right
- Numbness in the leg; worse on coughing and straining
- Worse sitting, relieved lying down; walking unrestricted
- No weakness, no red flags
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Below-knee radiation with numbness and a positive cough response, well beyond six weeks, fits a lumbar nerve-root pattern.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Straight-leg raise and dermatomal mapping
- Daily analgesic use and what he is taking
- He wrote *(translated)*: "I have to take medicine every day or I cannot work. Is there any permanent cure for this?" He is asking about cure, not management — worth answering directly.
amber_motor_deficit-002:
**Snapshot** — 42y woman, teacher. Lower back pain with weakness, 6 weeks to 3 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Difficulty standing on toes and heels; the leg feels weak
- Pain radiates to the thigh, above the knee
- Weakness reported as static, not rapidly progressing
- Walking unrestricted; no red flags
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Reported motor involvement without rapid progression warrants examination rather than same-day review.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Whether the weakness is genuine or pain-limited
- Power by myotome, comparing sides; reflexes and any wasting
- Whether it has changed at all this month
- She wrote *(translated)*: "I have been suffering a long time. I have to work and I cannot bear the pain either."
amber_stenosis-001:
**Snapshot** — 59y woman, retired. Lower back and bilateral leg pain with difficulty walking, more than a year.

**Key findings**
- Walking limited to 100–500 metres
- Relief on sitting or bending forward, not on standing still
- Pain to the buttocks both sides; nothing below the knee
- No numbness, weakness or red flags
- Painkillers only; no physiotherapy

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Walking-limited pain relieved by flexion, at 59, fits a neurogenic claudication pattern.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- She wrote *(translated)*: "Two years of lower back pain, worse when bending" — which reads against her answer that bending forward relieves the walking pain. Worth separating the two.
- Walking distance flat versus uphill, and whether cycling is easier
- Pulses and ankle-brachial index, to exclude a vascular cause
amber_cervical_radiculopathy-012:
**Snapshot** — 63y woman, Nashik. Neck pain with arm pain and numbness, 3 to 12 months, 7/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain radiates below the elbow into the left hand
- Numbness and tingling in the hand and fingers
- No dexterity loss, no gait change, no bilateral involvement
- Working with difficulty; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Arm pain below the elbow with hand numbness, well beyond six weeks, fits a nerve-root pattern rather than cord involvement.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Which fingers, to localise the root
- Spurling's test and upper-limb reflexes
- Whether the arm pain outweighs the neck pain
- She wrote *(translated)*: "I have been suffering a long time. I have to work and I cannot bear the pain either."
amber_failed_conservative-001:
**Snapshot** — 46y woman, desk job. Lower back pain for more than a year, 6/10, no radiation.

**Key findings**
- More than six weeks of physiotherapy with no benefit at all
- Work still affected
- Pain stays in the back — no numbness, weakness or red flags
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- No imaging

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Conservative care has been tried for an adequate period and failed, with function still impaired.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- What the physiotherapy involved, and whether it was supervised
- Whether anything changed the pain at all, even briefly
- She wrote *(translated)*: "I do not understand what I should do. I will do whatever you tell me." She will likely accept any plan offered, so the plan needs to be a considered one.
amber_post_surgical-009:
**Snapshot** — 57y woman, Bhopal. Lower back pain for more than a year, 5/10, no radiation.

**Key findings**
- Previous spine surgery about six years ago; she does not recall the level
- Physiotherapy 2 to 6 weeks, partial benefit
- Pain stays in the back — no leg symptoms or neurological findings
- No red flags; no imaging since
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Previous spine surgery makes this a revision assessment rather than a first presentation, whatever the current severity.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Operative notes — she cannot recall the level, so records matter more than history
- Whether there was a pain-free interval after surgery, and how long
- She wrote *(translated)*: "Lower back pain for two years, worse on bending" — which does not sit with an operation six years ago for the same problem
amber_functional_collapse-001:
**Snapshot** — 39y woman, desk job. Lower back pain for 3 to 12 months, 8/10, has stopped working.

**Key findings**
- Has had to stop work entirely
- Reports it is still getting worse
- Now needs some help with dressing and bathing
- Sleep disturbed most nights
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation or neurological findings

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Loss of work and continuing deterioration over months, with no neurological cause on the form, warrants a consult on its own.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- What specifically stopped her working, and when
- Mood and sleep, given the duration and the severity
- Whether anyone has examined her during this period
- She wrote *(translated)*: "I have been suffering a long time. I have to work and I cannot bear the pain either."
